attributes.measurements: Root-caused via target-asm evidence, not guesswork: grepped the target-vs-ours unified disasm diff for every `lwz rX,100(r31)` (offsetof(Effect,flags)=100) occurrence -- target reloads e->flags fresh via lwz+rlwinm. at 20+ distinct points scattered across the function's while/do-while/straight-line blocks, INCLUDING three points inside the enemy-collision `while ((enemyIndex = NextGridItem()) >= 0)` loop where our pre-fix build had HOISTED the bitmask test (flags&0x100, flags&0x1000000, flags&0x00800000) to a single pre-loop rlwinm + stw-to-stack-slot, then re-loaded the slot + cmplwi'd against 0 every iteration -- a textbook loop-invariant-code-motion divergence caused by `flags` being a real machine-level scalar local (never re-derived from memory) vs target's repeated e->flags memory reads. All `rlwinm.`-vs-`cmplwi`/`cmpwi` bit-test-vs-compare op-mismatches in the --ops diff (2 within the enemy loop, 1 later at the 0x00800000 site) resolved cleanly after the fix; grep for 'rlwinm' against the post-fix --ops diff returns zero remaining structural hits. The u32 cast fix independently closed one more cmpwi/cmplwi op-mismatch (target cmplwi, ours cmpwi, at the lbl_8023CB28+68 collision-flag test) with zero behavioral change (an != 0 test is signedness-independent at the C level).
attributes.policy: Confirmed `e` (the Effect* loop pointer, &page->fx[i]) genuinely escapes to many calls within the same outer for-loop iteration (GetWorldMat, CreateDirMatrix, PitchMat3/YawMat3/RollMat3, MBTreeSetAlpha, damage_enemy, PlayerDamagedEnemy, StartFXSub, etc.), so MWCC's alias analysis must treat e->flags as potentially clobbered after every call and reload fresh -- exactly what target's disassembly shows. Verified the local `flags` variable was write-once (only the removed initializer assigns it; grepped for any `flags =`/`flags &=`/`flags |=` beyond the initializer, found none) so deleting it and substituting e->flags at all 27 read sites is semantically inert (same value read, just re-derived from memory instead of a cached register/stack slot) -- confirmed by full rebuild + fndiff, no new op-mismatches introduced anywhere in the function. Also verified the sibling item-collision while loop (`while ((itemIndex = NextGridEnemy()) >= 0)`, lines ~3355-3424) ALREADY used e->flags directly at every site (never routed through the flags local) -- this pre-existing asymmetry within the same function was the strongest single tell that flags-caching, not e->flags-reading, was the reconstruction deviation from original source shape.
attributes.residual: Remaining --ops clusters (173) are dominated by the SAME function-wide MWCC constant/address-materialization prologue divergence already characterized in the superseded v1 record (target hoists ~20 float/double literal constants + ~8 global addresses into a single pre-loop block, kept resident across ~11 non-volatile FPRs; ours performs a similarly-scaled hoist but with a different stack-slot/interleave order) -- re-confirmed this session by direct fnasm inspection of both sides' prologues (offset 0x18-0x1c8 target / matching span ours): both sides hoist the SAME set of loop-invariant constants out of the same for-loop, just in different internal order, corroborating this is genuine MWCC PRE-heuristic nondeterminism, not a missing optimization.
